article.title: Oracle's Notes Call JDK 21.0.13, Dated October 20, the First JDK 21 Update Under the OTN License, With a Next Update Listed for November 17
article.summary: Oracle's release notes mark JDK 21.0.13 as the first JDK 21 update under the Java SE OTN license instead of the NFTC; the Herald compares Oracle's pages with InfoQ, The Register, Temurin and Corretto.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Oracle's consolidated release notes describe [JDK 21.0.13](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/21all-relnotes.html), dated October 20, 2026, as "the first JDK 21 update release made available under the Oracle Technology Network License Agreement for Oracle Java SE (OTN for Java SE)." The notes add that this license "is substantially different from the Oracle No-fee Terms and Conditions (NFTC) used in earlier JDK 21 updates." This analysis sets Oracle's own pages on the change (three blog posts, the release notes, a licensing FAQ and the support roadmap) beside what InfoQ, The Register, Eclipse Temurin and Amazon Corretto published, and it lists the places where the sources differ. It reports what the cited pages say and does not interpret the license text. The Herald has not covered the change before.

## Background

Oracle's [August 14, 2026 blog post](https://blogs.oracle.com/java/jdk-21-approaches-end-of-permissive-license), written by Donald Smith, Vice President of Product Management, set out the plan. It says the release of Oracle JDK 25 in September 2025 "started the one-year transition period for NFTC users of JDK 21," that "all updates through and including September 2026 are available under the NFTC," and that further updates, "beginning with the October 2026 Critical Patch Update (CPU), are planned to be offered under the Java SE OTN license." The same post says that GraalVM for JDK 21 updates are planned to move to a GraalVM OTN license from the October 2026 CPU.

The post lists groups that "will continue to be able to use the latest JDK 21 updates": Java SE Universal Subscription customers, legacy Java SE product customers, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure users, users of Oracle Java as part of licensed Oracle products, and users running Java for personal use, development, testing, prototyping or demonstrating applications. It adds that under the subscription, commercial support for Java 21 "remains available until at least September 2031."

Oracle's [licensing FAQ](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/jdk-faqs.html) states the split as a table. For Java 21, "releases after September 2026 (21.0.13 and later)" fall under My Oracle Support and the OTN license "for Personal, Development and other Users only," while "releases through September 2026 (21.0.12 and earlier)" fall under the NFTC "for All Users." The [support roadmap](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/java-se-support-roadmap.html), updated October 20, 2026, points to the same pattern for Java 17, whose updates "released as of October 15, 2024" are under the OTN license.

## Current situation

The dates below are Oracle's release-note dates, which carry no time zone.

- **August 18, 2026:** JDK 21.0.12.1. Its notes say that "update releases of Oracle JDK 21 after September of 2026 will switch to the Java SE OTN license."
- **October 20, 2026:** JDK 21.0.13, the release the notes mark as the first under OTN. The notes say it "contains fixes for security vulnerabilities described in the Oracle Critical Patch Update." [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/java-news-roundup-oct19-2026/) listed 21.0.13 among the JDK versions Oracle released with its October 2026 CPU.
- **October 21, 2026:** JDK 21.0.13.0.2, which the notes say stopped trusting the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. The Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-11/06-emudhra-ca-compromise-uv-shipped-fixes-october-20-and-21-an-aws-cli-fix-merged-october-21-azure-clis-certifi-pin-changed-in-2920-on-november-3) on how Python tooling and cloud command-line tools handled the same incident.
- **October 24, 2026:** JDK 21.0.13.0.3, whose notes cite the Oracle Security Alert Advisory for CVE-2026-114820.
- **November 17, 2026:** the 21.0.13, 21.0.13.0.2 and 21.0.13.0.3 notes each say the build is not recommended for use "after the next critical patch update scheduled for November 17, 2026." Oracle's [September 10 blog update](https://blogs.oracle.com/java/transitioning-java-to-more-frequent-security-updates) calls the same date a "Java CSPU" planned "in addition to our regularly scheduled October and January CPU releases," and says "We plan to provide multiple monthly updates in CY27."

Eclipse Temurin and Amazon Corretto also published 21.0.13 builds. Eclipse Temurin's GitHub repository shows [jdk-21.0.13+9](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries/releases/tag/jdk-21.0.13+9) published at 2026-10-22T08:58:06Z (UTC), after [jdk-21.0.12.1+1](https://github.com/adoptium/temurin21-binaries/releases/tag/jdk-21.0.12.1+1) at 2026-08-19T12:10:19Z. Amazon Corretto's [changelog](https://github.com/corretto/corretto-21/blob/21.0.13.0.11/CHANGELOG.md) dates 21.0.13.0.10 as October 20 and lists it as importing OpenJDK 21.0.13+9, and dates 21.0.13.0.11 as October 24 with CVE-2026-114820 at a CVSS score of 9.1. The GitHub release pages for the same two Corretto builds, [21.0.13.0.10](https://github.com/corretto/corretto-21/releases/tag/21.0.13.0.10) and [21.0.13.0.11](https://github.com/corretto/corretto-21/releases/tag/21.0.13.0.11), are timestamped 2026-10-23T05:53:31Z and 2026-10-27T00:08:25Z; neither source explains the gap, so both sets of dates are given. Corretto's [FAQ](https://aws.amazon.com/corretto/faqs/) says Corretto "is licensed under the terms of the GNU Public License version 2 with the Class Path Exception (GPLv2 with CPE)," and lists Corretto 21 with a last planned update of July 2030. InfoQ reported that Azul released October CPU patches covering 53 CVEs for Zulu 21 and other versions, and that BellSoft released CPU patches for Liberica JDK 21.0.12.1.1 together with a patch set update numbered 21.0.13.

On price, Oracle's [October 8 post](https://blogs.oracle.com/java/new-lower-smb-pricing-and-easier-online-purchasing-of-java-se-universal-subscription) announced annual Java SE Universal Subscription prices for organizations with fewer than 3,000 employees: $100 for 10 or fewer employees, $1,000 for 100 or fewer, $10,000 for 500 or fewer, and $147.20 for each additional employee from 501 to 2,999. Pricing for 3,000 or more employees is "Unchanged." The Register, in a [September 7 report on possible European Commission interest in Oracle's licensing](https://www.theregister.com/software/2026/09/07/oracle-may-be-next-in-eu-software-licensing-hot-seat-following-sap-deal/5294805), wrote that "Gartner estimated the per-employee subscription model to be two to five times more expensive than the legacy version." That article is about Oracle licensing generally and does not mention JDK 21.

## Where the sources differ

- **Which year the permissive updates ran to.** The support roadmap says "public updates through September 2025 were under a permissive license" for Java SE 21, in the same paragraph that dates the OTN releases from October 20, 2026. Oracle's blog post, FAQ and release notes say September 2026. The Herald found no explanation on the roadmap page and does not reconcile the two.
- **The last NFTC build.** A [DEV Community post](https://dev.to/jamilxt/oracle-jdk-21-goes-paid-on-october-20-temurin-vs-corretto-vs-jdk-25-and-how-to-choose-28fo) published September 25 calls 21.0.12, dated July 21, "the last free-for-production JDK 21 build." Oracle's notes list the later 21.0.12.1, dated August 18, and the FAQ's NFTC row names "21.0.12 and earlier" without naming 21.0.12.1.
- **What November 17 is called.** The release notes call it a critical patch update; the September 10 blog update calls it a Java CSPU in addition to the CPUs.
- **Corretto's dates.** The changelog and the GitHub release timestamps differ, as noted above.

## Implications

What follows is drawn from the cited pages. Oracle's FAQ says "You may continue to use releases you have downloaded under the terms of the license under which you downloaded them." Its 21.0.12.1 notes say "Users wishing to receive updates of the Oracle JDK under the free Java license should migrate to Oracle JDK 25." For JDK 25, the blog post says NFTC updates are planned "until October 2028," while the FAQ says "until September of 2028"; both tie the end to one year after Java 29.

Because the 21.0.13, 21.0.13.0.2 and 21.0.13.0.3 notes advise against use after November 17, that date is the next point at which those builds are no longer recommended by Oracle. Whether Oracle labels it a CPU or a CSPU, the September 10 post says organizations "should be preparing" for monthly updates in 2027.

For teams that run OpenJDK-based builds, the cited distributor pages show Temurin and Corretto publishing 21.0.13 builds within days of Oracle's, and Corretto listing the CVE-2026-114820 fix under its October 24 changelog date. The Temurin release page names only the version, so it does not show whether that build carries the fix.
